neighbours.label: the verb right after a quoted or named term used as subject in a definitional statement: "the term 'X' has/is", "the two fields didn't"
fire: The phrase 'free range' has no strict legal meaning.
In this sense, the term 'theory' is used very loosely.
The word 'gift' does not mean the same thing in German.
Biologists say the label 'species' has fuzzy edges.
The expression 'cold turkey' is of uncertain origin.
Technically, the name 'peanut' is misleading, since it is a legume.
The concept of 'race' has no clear basis in genetics.
Note that the term 'organic' does not apply to fish.
quiet: The farm sells free range eggs at the Sunday market.
In this sense, the scientists used theory very carefully.
She gave him a small gift when she visited Germany.
Biologists counted every species along the river edges.
He quit smoking cold turkey after his father fell ill.
Technically, peanuts grow underground, since they are legumes.
The race was held in heavy rain on Saturday morning.
Note that organic fish costs more at most shops.

short: predicate after a term as subject
notes: Card mixes ' is', ' has', ' fields', ' frames'. Probes of quoted-term subjects reached only 0.06-0.13. Expect fail.
